```{ojs}
//| echo: false
buildQuiz = function(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="margin:18px 0 24px 0;text-align:center;">
    <button style="
      display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;
      background:linear-gradient(135deg,#667eea 0%,#764ba2 100%);
      color:#fff;border:none;padding:9px 22px;border-radius:50px;
      font-size:.95em;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;
      box-shadow:0 3px 12px rgba(102,126,234,.45);
      transition:transform .15s,box-shadow .15s;"
      onmouseover="this.style.transform='scale(1.04)';this.style.boxShadow='0 5px 18px rgba(102,126,234,.55)'"
      onmouseout="this.style.transform='scale(1)';this.style.boxShadow='0 3px 12px rgba(102,126,234,.45)'"
    >
      <span style="font-size:1.1em;">📝</span> ${title}
      <span class="chevron" style="transition:transform .3s;">▼</span>
    </button>
    <div class="quiz-body" style="
      max-height:0;opacity:0;overflow:hidden;
      transition:max-height .5s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1),opacity .4s ease,margin-top .3s ease;
      margin-top:0;text-align:left;">
      <button class="close-btn" style="
        display:block;margin:0 auto 10px auto;
        background:rgba(102,126,234,.12);color:#667eea;border:none;
        padding:5px 18px;border-radius:50px;font-size:.85em;
        font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;">Hide Quiz</button>
      <p style="text-align:center;color:#718096;font-style:italic;font-size:.9em;margin-bottom:12px;">
        Select an answer for each question.</p>
    </div>
  </div>`;
  const toggle = outer.querySelector("button");
  const chevron = toggle.querySelector(".chevron");
  const body   = outer.querySelector(".quiz-body");
  const closeBtn = body.querySelector(".close-btn");
  function expand(){  body.style.maxHeight="2000px";body.style.opacity="1";body.style.marginTop="14px";chevron.style.transform="rotate(180deg)"; }
  function collapse(){ body.style.maxHeight="0";body.style.opacity="0";body.style.marginTop="0";chevron.style.transform="rotate(0)"; }
  toggle.onclick = () => body.style.maxHeight === "0px" || body.style.maxHeight === "" ? expand() : collapse();
  closeBtn.onclick = collapse;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;transition:border-color .2s,background .2s;";
      btn.onmouseover = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#667eea";btn.style.background="#f0f0ff"; }};
      btn.onmouseout  = () => { if(!card.dataset.answered){ btn.style.borderColor="#e2e8f0";btn.style.background="#fff"; }};
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if(card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => { b.style.cursor="default"; b.onmouseover=null; b.onmouseout=null; });
        if(oi === qq.correct){
          btn.style.borderColor="#48bb78";btn.style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#276749";fb.style.background="#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor="#fc8181";btn.style.background="#fff5f5";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.borderColor="#48bb78";
          card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct].style.background="#f0fff4";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation;
          fb.style.color="#9b2c2c";fb.style.background="#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding="10px 14px";fb.style.marginTop="8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;transition:all .3s;";
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  return outer;
}
```

# Anchor Phenomenon: Earth's Temperature Is Rising {#anchor-phenomenon}

::: {.engage-box}
## 🌍 A 2,000-year trend, reversed

<div style="font-size: 1.2em; font-weight: 700; text-align: center; margin: 18px 0;">
Earth's temperature is rising, reversing the cooling trend that occurred over the past 2,000 years, putting millions of people in harm's way, yet the public is not convinced of the risks.
</div>

- You started talking about climate change in **Unit 1**, and you have probably heard a lot about it in the news.
- While climate has changed in the past because of **natural factors**, **99.9%** of climate research agrees that today's warming is different: **humans are the cause**.
- That also means humans can take action to reduce the changes and their consequences. But that takes a public that understands the problem.
:::

**Think about it** (your teacher asks these at the start of the unit):

- What **effects** does climate change have on humans and the natural environment?
- What is your current understanding of what is **causing** climate change?
- How do you think lingering **skepticism** (doubt) can affect our ability to respond to climate change?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 💬 Ideas classmates often share (try your own first!)

**Effects:** species dying out faster; fish that people eat changing where they migrate; low-lying islands and cities going under water as sea level rises; more droughts, wildfires, extreme heat, and storms.

**Causes:** burning fossil fuels makes greenhouse gases; other greenhouse gases from humans; natural factors could also play a part; "the Sun is getting stronger"; "the hole in the ozone layer."

Some of these ideas hold up and some don't. This unit is about checking each one against the data, the same way scientists do.
:::

### 🎬 Videos from class

Your teacher showed these two videos before the Tell the Story texts. As you watch, notice **how people describe feeling climate change**, and **why people are being forced to leave their homes**.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Saved "circled" details, shared by the three texts and the Detail Tracker. Kept in localStorage when it is available.
u4oDetails = {
  const KEY = "u4o-tell-the-story-v1";
  let state = {details: [], story: ""};
  try {
    const saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY));
    if (saved && Array.isArray(saved.details)) state = {details: saved.details, story: saved.story || ""};
  } catch (e) {}
  const subs = [];
  const persist = () => { try { localStorage.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(state)); } catch (e) {} };
  const notify = () => {
    persist();
    for (let i = subs.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      const s = subs[i];
      if (s.el.isConnected) s.seen = true;
      else if (s.seen) { subs.splice(i, 1); continue; }
      s.fn();
    }
  };
  return {
    has: id => state.details.some(d => d.id === id),
    list: () => state.details.slice(),
    toggle: d => {
      state.details = state.details.some(x => x.id === d.id) ? state.details.filter(x => x.id !== d.id) : [...state.details, d];
      notify();
    },
    remove: id => { state.details = state.details.filter(x => x.id !== id); notify(); },
    story: () => state.story,
    setStory: t => { state.story = t; persist(); },
    clear: () => { state = {details: [], story: ""}; notify(); },
    // fn re-runs on every change until el has been attached to the page and then removed
    subscribe: (el, fn) => subs.push({el, fn, seen: false})
  };
}
```

## Text 1: Arctic (above 65° north) Summer Temperature Over Last 2000 Years {#text-1}

From your PTO:

- The **y-axis** is the difference **compared** to the average temperature (0 means "no different from normal").
- The **blue line** shows estimates of temperatures over the last 2,000 years, based on records from **lake sediments, ice cores and tree rings** ("indirect measurement").
- The **red line** shows the recent warming based on **actual observations** (thermometers, "direct measurement after 1880").

Tap a time period to zoom in on it, and hover over or tap the graph to read values.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Values read by eye from the PTO's graph ("Global temperature over the past two millennia"), every 20 years.
// They are approximate: the real record has more year-to-year wiggles than this.
u4oBlue = [
  [0, .02], [20, .12], [40, .06], [60, .10], [80, .04], [100, .11], [120, .07], [140, .03], [160, .12], [180, .08],
  [200, .10], [220, .05], [240, .22], [260, .10], [280, .14], [300, .08], [320, .06], [340, .12], [360, .04], [380, .10],
  [400, .15], [420, .07], [440, .11], [460, .05], [480, .12], [500, .06], [520, .04], [540, -.14], [560, .06], [580, .10],
  [600, .13], [620, .05], [640, .10], [660, .16], [680, .06], [700, -.12], [720, .10], [740, .14], [760, .20], [780, .08],
  [800, .12], [820, .06], [840, .15], [860, .10], [880, .04], [900, .11], [920, .18], [940, .07], [960, .10], [980, .05],
  [1000, .12], [1020, .08], [1040, .06], [1060, .10], [1080, .04], [1100, .07], [1120, .02], [1140, .06], [1160, .09], [1180, .03],
  [1200, .05], [1220, -.02], [1240, .03], [1260, -.10], [1280, -.02], [1300, .02], [1320, -.03], [1340, .01], [1360, -.04], [1380, .00],
  [1400, -.02], [1420, -.06], [1440, -.10], [1460, -.24], [1480, -.08], [1500, -.05], [1520, -.12], [1540, -.07], [1560, -.10], [1580, -.15],
  [1600, -.26], [1620, -.12], [1640, -.22], [1660, -.14], [1680, -.18], [1700, -.28], [1720, -.12], [1740, -.08], [1760, -.14], [1780, -.17],
  [1800, -.12], [1820, -.30], [1840, -.18], [1860, -.10], [1880, -.08]
].map(([year, t]) => ({year, t, kind: "Indirect (lake sediments, ice cores, tree rings)"}))
u4oRed = [
  [1880, .08], [1890, -.05], [1900, -.10], [1910, -.22], [1920, -.08], [1930, .02], [1940, .25], [1950, .05], [1960, .12],
  [1970, .10], [1980, .30], [1990, .45], [2000, .60], [2010, .85], [2015, 1.0], [2020, 1.2]
].map(([year, t]) => ({year, t, kind: "Direct measurement (thermometers)"}))
u4oMean = (arr, a, b) => d3.mean(arr.filter(d => d.year >= a && d.year <= b), d => d.t)
u4oRates = {
  const cool = (u4oMean(u4oBlue, 1760, 1860) - u4oMean(u4oBlue, 1000, 1100)) / 7.6;
  const warm = (u4oMean(u4oRed, 2010, 2020) - u4oMean(u4oRed, 1890, 1910)) / 1.2;
  return {cool, warm};
}
u4oEras = [
  {id: "all", label: "All 2,000 years", x1: 0, x2: 2025, color: "#475569", details: [
    {id: "t1-all-flat", label: "2,000 years", detail: "For about 1,800 years the blue line stays within about 0.3 °C of zero."},
    {id: "t1-all-spike", label: "2,000 years", detail: "The red line shoots up to about +1.2 °C, far higher than any point on the blue line in 2,000 years."}
  ]},
  {id: "early", label: "Year 0–1000", x1: 0, x2: 1000, color: "#1d4ed8", details: [
    {id: "t1-early-warm", label: "Year 0–1000", detail: "From year 0 to about 1000, temperatures wiggled up and down but stayed a little above zero (about +0.1 °C)."},
    {id: "t1-early-dips", label: "Year 0–1000", detail: "Sharp dips that last only a few years (like around 540 CE) line up with huge volcanic eruptions that briefly blocked sunlight."}
  ]},
  {id: "cool", label: "1000–1850: slow cooling", x1: 1000, x2: 1850, color: "#0891b2", details: [
    {id: "t1-cool-trend", label: "1000–1850", detail: "After about 1000, the blue line slowly drifts down. By the 1800s Earth was about 0.2–0.3 °C cooler."},
    {id: "t1-cool-slow", label: "1000–1850", detail: "This cooling was slow: only about 0.03 °C per 100 years, over hundreds of years."}
  ]},
  {id: "recent", label: "1850–today: the red line", x1: 1850, x2: 2025, color: "#dc2626", details: [
    {id: "t1-recent-rise", label: "1850–today", detail: "Thermometer records (red) start in 1880. Since about 1900, temperature rose about 1.2 °C in just over 100 years."},
    {id: "t1-recent-reverse", label: "1850–today", detail: "The recent warming reversed about 1,000 years of slow cooling, and it is about 30 times faster."},
    {id: "t1-recent-2024", label: "1850–today", detail: "2024 was the warmest year on record, about 1.55 °C above the late 1800s (WMO)."}
  ]}
]
u4oText1State = ({era: "all", add2024: false})
```

```{ojs}
  const input = cb.querySelector("input");
  input.checked = st.add2024;
  const fire = () => { wrap.value = {era: st.era, add2024: st.add2024}; draw(); wrap.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true})); };
  input.onchange = () => { st.add2024 = input.checked; fire(); };
  const draw = () => chips.replaceChildren(...u4oEras.map(e => u4oChip(e.label, e.id === st.era, e.color, () => { st.era = e.id; fire(); })), cb);
  draw();
  wrap.appendChild(chips);
  return wrap;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 🔎 About this graph: Arctic or global?

The PTO's heading and bullets describe **Arctic summer temperatures** compared with the **2,000-year average**. The graph itself is labeled **"Global temperature over the past two millennia"**, measured as **change from pre-industrial** (the late 1800s). Both kinds of records tell the same story: a long, slow cooling, then a sudden, steep warming. In the Arctic the recent warming is even **bigger**, because the Arctic is warming about **3 to 4 times faster** than the world as a whole. The values on this page were read by eye from the PTO graph, so they are approximate.
:::

```{ojs}
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "The past wiggles stay within about ±0.3 °C. The red line climbs about 1.2 °C in roughly 100 years, around 30 times faster than the long cooling."
  }
```

## Text 2: Climate-Related Human Displacement in 2023 {#text-2}

Text #2 is an **Al Jazeera** graphic built from data from the **Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC, 2024)**: *"Where have weather-related events caused the most displacement?"* A **displacement** is when someone is forced to leave their home. Tap a circle or a country to read about it.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
u4oWorld = {
  const topojson = await require("topojson-client@3.1.0");
  try {
    const t = await d3.json("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2.0.2/countries-110m.json");
    return {countries: topojson.feature(t, t.objects.countries).features, land: topojson.feature(t, t.objects.land)};
  } catch (e) {
    try {
      const t = await d3.json("../world-110m.json");
      const key = t.objects.land ? "land" : Object.keys(t.objects)[0];
      return {countries: [], land: topojson.feature(t, t.objects[key])};
    } catch (e2) {
      return {countries: [], land: null};
    }
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof u4oCountryPick = {
  const w = width, k = Math.max(0.6, Math.min(1, w / 700));
  const st = u4oText2State;
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.value = st.pick;
  const box = {type: "MultiPoint", coordinates: [[-20, -38], [-20, 0], [-20, 58], [65, -38], [65, 58], [150, -38], [150, 0], [150, 58]]};
  const projection = d3.geoEqualEarth().rotate([-65, 0]).fitWidth(w, box);
  const path = d3.geoPath(projection);
  const h = Math.ceil(path.bounds(box)[1][1]);
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, w, h]).attr("width", w).attr("height", h)
    .style("max-width", "100%").style("height", "auto").style("display", "block").style("border-radius", "10px")
    .attr("role", "img").attr("aria-label", "Map of Africa and Asia showing weather-related displacement in 2023. The biggest circles are in China, the Philippines, Somalia, Bangladesh, and Myanmar.");
  svg.append("rect").attr("width", w).attr("height", h).attr("fill", "#111827");
  const hit = new Set(u4oDisplaced.map(d => d.id));
  if (u4oWorld.countries.length) {
    svg.append("g").selectAll("path").data(u4oWorld.countries).join("path")
      .attr("d", path).attr("fill", d => hit.has(d.id) ? "#fde7c3" : "#e5e7eb").attr("stroke", "#9ca3af").attr("stroke-width", 0.4);
  } else if (u4oWorld.land) {
    svg.append("path").attr("d", path(u4oWorld.land)).attr("fill", "#e5e7eb");
  }
  const r = d3.scaleSqrt().domain([0, 4573773]).range([0, 34 * k]);
  const marks = svg.append("g");
  wrap.appendChild(svg.node());
  const list = document.createElement("div");
  list.style.cssText = "margin-top:10px;display:grid;gap:6px;";
  wrap.appendChild(list);
  const draw = () => {
    marks.selectAll("*").remove();
    for (const d of [...u4oDisplaced].sort((a, b) => (a.country === wrap.value) - (b.country === wrap.value) || b.n - a.n)) {
      const on = d.country === wrap.value;
      const [x, y] = projection([d.lon, d.lat]);
      const g = marks.append("g").style("cursor", "pointer").attr("tabindex", 0).attr("role", "button").attr("aria-label", `${d.country}: ${d.n.toLocaleString()} displacements`)
        .on("click", () => pick(d.country)).on("keydown", e => { if (e.key === "Enter" || e.key === " ") { e.preventDefault(); pick(d.country); } });
      g.append("title").text(`${d.country}: ${d.n.toLocaleString()}`);
      g.append("circle").attr("cx", x).attr("cy", y).attr("r", r(d.n)).attr("fill", "#f59e0b").attr("fill-opacity", on ? 0.9 : 0.6)
        .attr("stroke", on ? "#fff" : "#b45309").attr("stroke-width", on ? 3 : 1);
      if (w >= 520) g.append("text").attr("x", x).attr("y", y - r(d.n) - 5).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 11 * k).attr("font-weight", 800)
        .attr("fill", "#fff").attr("paint-order", "stroke").attr("stroke", "#111827").attr("stroke-width", 3).style("pointer-events", "none").text(d.country);
    }
    const max = u4oDisplaced[0].n;
    list.replaceChildren(...u4oDisplaced.map(d => {
      const on = d.country === wrap.value;
      const row = document.createElement("button");
      row.type = "button";
      row.setAttribute("aria-pressed", on);
      row.style.cssText = `display:block;text-align:left;width:100%;min-height:44px;padding:6px 10px;border-radius:8px;cursor:pointer;color:#1e1b4b;border:2px solid ${on ? "#d97706" : "#e2e8f0"};background:${on ? "#fffbeb" : "#fff"};`;
      row.innerHTML = `<b>${d.country}</b> · ${d.n.toLocaleString()} displacements
        <span style="display:block;height:8px;margin-top:4px;border-radius:4px;background:#f59e0b;width:${(100 * d.n / max).toFixed(1)}%;"></span>`;
      row.onclick = () => pick(d.country);
      return row;
    }));
  };
  const pick = c => { wrap.value = st.pick = c; draw(); wrap.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true})); };
  draw();
  const legend = document.createElement("div");
  legend.style.cssText = "font-size:.85em;text-align:center;margin-top:6px;";
  legend.innerHTML = `Circle area = number of displacements. The map is zoomed in on Africa and Asia, where the labeled countries are. Only the five countries labeled on the PTO graphic are shown; the PTO map also has many smaller, unlabeled circles. Source: Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (2024), via Al Jazeera.`;
  wrap.appendChild(legend);
  return wrap;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 🔎 People vs. displacements

**6.6 million people** and **20.3 million displacements** are both correct. One family can be forced out by a flood in July, return, and then be forced out again by a typhoon in September. That counts as two displacements but the same people. The 20.3 million counts only **weather-related** disasters; earthquakes (like the 2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes) are counted separately.
:::

```{ojs}
    explanation: "Floods (9.8 million) and storms (9.5 million) together made up about 95% of the 20.3 million displacements."
  },
  {
    q: "Where were the biggest numbers of displacements?",

    explanation: "Four of the five labeled countries are in South and East Asia, where many people live on low coasts and river deltas that typhoons, cyclones and floods hit."

    correct: 1,
    explanation: "A displacement is counted each time someone is forced to leave. Repeated floods and storms forced many people out several times."
  }
])
```

## Text 3: Scientist vs. Public Opinions of Climate Change {#text-3}

Text #3 is an infographic: **"How do scientists think about climate change? What about the public?"** Before you look, make a guess.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const box = html`<div style="background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin:10px 0;box-shadow:0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.1);">
    <div style="font-weight:800;margin-bottom:6px;">🤔 Guess first: What percent of people in the U.S. <i>think that scientists agree</i> that climate change is caused by human activities?</div>
    <div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:10px;align-items:center;">
      <input type="range" min="0" max="100" step="1" value="50" style="flex:1 1 200px;min-height:36px;" aria-label="Your guess, in percent">
      <b class="val" style="min-width:3em;">50%</b>
      <button type="button" style="min-height:40px;padding:6px 16px;border:none;border-radius:50px;background:#0f766e;color:#fff;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;">Reveal</button>
    </div>
    <div class="out" style="margin-top:8px;"></div>
  </div>`;
  const inp = box.querySelector("input"), val = box.querySelector(".val"), out = box.querySelector(".out");
  inp.oninput = () => val.textContent = inp.value + "%";
  box.querySelector("button").onclick = () => {
    const g = +inp.value, diff = Math.abs(g - 57);
    out.innerHTML = `<div style="padding:10px 12px;border-radius:8px;background:#f0fdfa;">Only <b>57%</b> of people think scientists agree. You guessed ${g}% (${diff <= 5 ? "very close!" : diff <= 15 ? "close" : "not too close"}). Meanwhile, <b>99.9%</b> of research papers agree. That gap is the problem this unit's performance task asks you to tackle.</div>`;
  };
  return box;
}
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 🔎 About these numbers

The **99.9%** comes from a study that checked over 88,000 peer-reviewed climate research papers (Lynas et al., 2021, reported in the Cornell Chronicle). The public numbers come from surveys of U.S. adults (Pew Research and Yale Climate Change Communication), and the 88% of scientists from a survey in *Nature Human Behaviour*. The PTO's Performance Task Introduction rounds them: **over 40%** doubt human involvement (29% + 12% = 41%) and about **one-third** are unconcerned (37%).
:::

::: {.key-idea}
### 💡 One way to tell the story

For nearly **2,000 years**, temperatures were slowly **declining**. Since around **1850**, they have been **rising dramatically**, about 1.2 °C in roughly a century. Climate and weather-related events **displaced millions of people in 2023**, mostly from **floods and storms**. A huge majority of scientists agree that **humans are causing climate change and that it is a problem**, but much of the public thinks the reality and cause of climate change are still uncertain.
:::

### 🤔 Questions this story raises

These are the questions that drive the rest of the unit, and where you will investigate them:

| Question | Where you'll investigate it |
|---|---|
| Why was Earth's temperature cooling before, but is rising now? | [Earth-Sun Dynamics](unit4-earth-sun-dynamics.qmd), [Climate Feedbacks](unit4-climate-feedbacks.qmd) |
| Why are scientists sure that humans are causing climate change? | [Earth-Sun Dynamics](unit4-earth-sun-dynamics.qmd), [Climate Feedbacks](unit4-climate-feedbacks.qmd) |
| Has the climate ever changed before? If so, how did it affect populations? | [The Past and the Future](unit4-past-and-future.qmd) |
| Why are people being displaced by climate factors? How will climate change affect people now and in the future? | [The Past and the Future](unit4-past-and-future.qmd) |
| Why are scientists so sure that climate change is a big deal? | [The Past and the Future](unit4-past-and-future.qmd), [Unit Closing](unit4-closing.qmd) |

# Performance Task Introduction {#performance-task-introduction}

::: {.explore-box}
## 📣 Educating your Community about the Predicted Impacts of Climate Change on Human Populations

Climate change, a scientifically proven phenomenon with dire consequences, faces significant public skepticism despite overwhelming consensus among experts.

While global efforts intensify, political leaders are not taking enough action to adequately address the challenge. **Urgent public demand is crucial** to motivating leaders into meaningful climate policies. This will require educating individuals to grasp **why experts overwhelmingly blame human actions**, specifically **greenhouse gas emissions**, for climate shifts, and **what negative effects** will likely result from these shifts.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="u4o-stats">
  <div class="u4o-stat" style="background:#0f766e;"><b>99.9%</b><span>of climate research attributes global warming to human activities</span></div>
  <div class="u4o-stat" style="background:#b45309;"><b>40%+</b><span>of U.S. citizens doubt that humans are involved</span></div>
  <div class="u4o-stat" style="background:#b91c1c;"><b>⅓</b><span>of U.S. citizens are unconcerned about its repercussions</span></div>
</div>
```

**Turn and talk** (or think on your own): Why do you think so many U.S. citizens don't believe humans are the cause of climate change, and about one-third aren't concerned, even though scientists agree and are worried?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## 💬 Ideas classmates often share

Social media · misinformation from people who deny climate change · politicians · some people think it's caused by natural factors · most people don't understand what scientists understand.

That last one is something **you** can change. That's the point of the performance task.
:::

::: {.key-idea}
### 🎯 Your task in this unit

Communicate the validity of the scientific consensus around the cause and importance of climate change. To do so, you will:

1. **Analyze and interpret data** to confirm scientists' understanding of **human activities as the cause** of climate change in this moment in time
2. **Analyze and interpret data** to determine **future impacts** of climate change
3. **Explain how these impacts** are expected to **affect human populations**
:::

### Revisiting the Performance Task

After each lesson, you'll return to your PTO and use that lesson's evidence for a **"Disproving climate skeptics"** prompt:

| After this lesson | Your PTO prompt asks you to make and support a claim about... |
|---|---|
| [Earth-Sun Dynamics](unit4-earth-sun-dynamics.qmd) (p. 9) | ...the role of **orbital factors and solar cycles** on the melting of ice caps today |
| [Climate Feedbacks](unit4-climate-feedbacks.qmd) (p. 10) | ...the role of **carbon dioxide and human activities** on the warming of the planet today |
| [The Past and the Future](unit4-past-and-future.qmd) (p. 11) | ...how **human populations** will likely be impacted by **climate-related hazards** in the near future |

**Final Performance Task (p. 12): Share with the community.** In a letter, public service announcement, pamphlet, or other format, communicate with someone in your community who is skeptical about climate change: (1) explain how the data demonstrates **human causes**, (2) describe the **ongoing and future impacts** on the planet, and (3) explain how these changes are likely to **affect people in your community**. See the [Unit Closing](unit4-closing.qmd).

# Initial Model {#initial-model}

::: {.explain-box}
## 🧩 What factors are contributing to climate change, and how is that resulting in human displacement?

Your first step is to develop an **initial model** that illustrates **different climate factors** and **how those factors impact average global temperatures**, and then how the resulting climate change could cause the **displacements** you saw in Text 2.
:::

### 🗣️ Rumors: What factors change a planet's temperature?

In class, everyone writes the climate factor idea they feel most confident about on a sticky note, and the class shares and sorts all the "rumors." Here is a virtual version. The question is: **What factors impact temperature and change in temperature on Earth and other planets and objects?** Think about what you learned in Units 1 and 2.

Sort each idea that classmates often suggest. Then tap **Show what scientists found** to compare. There is no score; it's OK to disagree for now, because you'll test these ideas in the lessons ahead.

```{ojs}
  {id: "volcano", f: "Volcanic eruptions", sci: "past", found: "Big eruptions release ash and gases that block sunlight and cool Earth for 1–3 years (the sharp dips in Text 1).   {id: "land", f: "Geography: land and landforms (where the continents and mountains are)", sci: "past", found: "The positions of continents and mountains shape climate, but they change over millions of years as plates move (Unit 3!), not over a century.", where: "Unit 3 connection", link: null},
  {id: "location", f: "Location on Earth (latitude: near the equator or near the poles)", sci: "past", found: "Latitude controls how much sunlight a place gets and causes seasons. It explains why places have different climates, not why the whole planet's average is rising.", where: "Seasons (Optional)", link: "unit4-seasons-optional.qmd"},
  {id: "asteroid", f: "Asteroid impacts", sci: "past", found: "A huge impact can change climate suddenly (it helped end the dinosaurs, Unit 2!). No large impact has happened in the past 2,000 years.", where: "Unit 2 connection", link: null},
  {id: "ozone", f: "The hole in the ozone layer", sci: "no", found: "A common mix-up. The ozone hole lets in more harmful UV light, which is a different problem. It is not a major cause of global warming.", where: "Climate Feedbacks", link: "unit4-climate-feedbacks.qmd"},
  {id: "hotsun", f: "The Sun is getting hotter and stronger", sci: "no", found: "Satellite measurements since 1978 show the Sun's energy has stayed about the same (even dipped slightly) while Earth warmed quickly.", where: "Earth-Sun Dynamics", link: "unit4-earth-sun-dynamics.qmd"}
]
u4oBins = [
  {id: "today", label: "🔥 Likely cause of today's warming", short: "Likely today", color: "#b91c1c"},
  {id: "past", label: "🕰️ Changes climate, but maybe not today's", short: "Not today's", color: "#1d4ed8"},
  {id: "unsure", label: "❓ Not sure yet", short: "Not sure", color: "#6b7280"}
]
u4oSciLabel = ({today: "Scientists identify this as the main cause of today's warming.", past: "Can change climate, but not the cause of today's warming.", amplify: "Makes warming bigger (a feedback), once something else starts it.", no: "Not a major cause of climate change."})
u4oSortState = ({picks: {}})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof u4oSort = {
  const st = u4oSortState;
  const wrap = html`<div style="margin:10px 0;"></div>`;
  wrap.value = {...st.picks};
  const tally = html`<div style="text-align:center;font-weight:700;margin:8px 0 14px;"></div>`;
  wrap.appendChild(tally);
  const paintTally = () => tally.textContent = `Sorted: ${Object.keys(st.picks).length} / ${u4oFactors.length}`;
  paintTally();
  for (const item of u4oFactors) {
    const card = html`<div style="background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:14px 16px;margin-bottom:12px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.1);">
      <div style="font-weight:700;margin-bottom:8px;">${item.f}</div>
      <div class="btns" style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;"></div>
      <button type="button" class="show" style="margin-top:8px;min-height:36px;padding:4px 14px;border:none;border-radius:50px;background:#ede9fe;color:#5b21b6;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;">Show what scientists found ▾</button>
      <div class="fb" style="font-size:.92em;"></div>
    </div>`;
    const btns = card.querySelector(".btns"), fb = card.querySelector(".fb"), show = card.querySelector(".show");
    const paint = () => btns.querySelectorAll("button").forEach((b, i) => {
      const bin = u4oBins[i], on = st.picks[item.id] === bin.id;
      b.style.background = on ? bin.color : "#fff"; b.style.color = on ? "#fff" : bin.color;
      b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", on);
    });
    for (const bin of u4oBins) {
      const b = html`<button type="button" style="flex:1 1 150px;min-height:44px;border:2px solid ${bin.color};border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:${bin.color};font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;font-size:.9em;">${bin.label}</button>`;
      b.onclick = () => {
        st.picks[item.id] = bin.id;
        paint(); paintTally();
        wrap.value = {...st.picks};
        wrap.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
      };
      btns.appendChild(b);
    }
    paint();
    show.onclick = () => {
      const open = fb.innerHTML !== "";
      if (open) { fb.innerHTML = ""; fb.style.cssText = "font-size:.92em;"; show.textContent = "Show what scientists found ▾"; return; }
      show.textContent = "Hide ▴";
      fb.style.cssText = "margin-top:8px;padding:10px 12px;border-radius:8px;background:#f5f3ff;color:#1e1b4b;font-size:.92em;";
      const where = item.link ? `<a href="${item.link}">${item.where}</a>` : item.where;
      fb.innerHTML = `<b>${u4oSciLabel[item.sci]}</b> ${item.found}<br><span style="font-size:.95em;">🔎 Investigate it: ${where}</span>`;
    };
    wrap.appendChild(card);
  }
  return wrap;
}
```

### 🛠️ Build your initial model

Your sort feeds this model sketch. Pick the effects you think warming could cause, then copy the sketch as a starting point for the drawing in your packet.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
u4oModelState = ({effects: new Set(["Floods", "Storms"])})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const st = u4oModelState;
  const effects = ["Floods", "Storms", "Droughts", "Wildfires", "Sea level rise", "Extreme heat"];
  const causes = u4oFactors.filter(f => u4oSort[f.id] === "today");
  const others = u4oFactors.filter(f => u4oSort[f.id] === "past" || u4oSort[f.id] === "unsure");
  const wrap = html`<div style="background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin:10px 0 18px;box-shadow:0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.1);"></div>`;
  const box = (title, color, inner) => `<div style="flex:1 1 200px;border:2px solid ${color};border-radius:10px;padding:10px 12px;"><div style="font-weight:800;color:${color};margin-bottom:4px;">${title}</div>${inner}</div>`;
  const arrow = `<div style="flex:0 0 auto;align-self:center;font-size:1.6em;font-weight:800;color:#1e1b4b;">→</div>`;
  const flow = html`<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;align-items:stretch;"></div>`;
  const effChips = html`<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px;"></div>`;
  const out = html`<div></div>`;
  const render = () => {
    const causeList = causes.length ? "<ul style='margin:0;padding-left:18px;'>" + causes.map(c => `<li>${c.f}</li>`).join("") + "</ul>" : "<i>Sort some factors as 🔥 Likely cause above.</i>";
    const eff = [...st.effects];
    flow.innerHTML = box("1. Climate factors", "#b91c1c", causeList) + arrow
      + box("2. Change in climate", "#c2410c", "Earth's average temperature rises") + arrow
      + box("3. Hazards", "#b45309", eff.length ? eff.join(", ") : "<i>Pick some effects below.</i>") + arrow
      + box("4. People", "#0f766e", "Homes damaged or unsafe → people displaced (forced to move)");
    effChips.replaceChildren(...effects.map(e => u4oChip(e, st.effects.has(e), "#b45309", () => { st.effects.has(e) ? st.effects.delete(e) : st.effects.add(e); render(); })));
    out.dataset.text = `My initial model\n1. Climate factors I think are causing today's warming: ${causes.map(c => c.f).join("; ") || "(none chosen yet)"}\n`
      + `   Other factors that can change climate (maybe not today's): ${others.map(c => c.f).join("; ") || "(none)"}\n`
      + `2. → Earth's average temperature rises\n3. → Hazards: ${eff.join(", ") || "(none chosen yet)"}\n4. → Homes are damaged or unsafe, so people are displaced (forced to move)`;
  };
  render();
  wrap.appendChild(flow);
  wrap.appendChild(html`<div style="font-weight:700;margin:12px 0 6px;">Effects of warming I want to show:</div>`);
  wrap.appendChild(effChips);
  const btn = html`<button type="button" style="margin-top:12px;min-height:40px;padding:6px 16px;border:none;border-radius:50px;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#667eea 0%,#764ba2 100%);color:#fff;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;">📋 Copy my model sketch</button>`;
  const msg = html`<span style="margin-left:8px;font-size:.9em;"></span>`;
  btn.onclick = async () => {
    try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(out.dataset.text); msg.textContent = "✅ Copied!"; }
    catch (e) { msg.textContent = "⚠️ Couldn't copy here. Copy it into your packet by hand."; }
  };
  wrap.appendChild(btn); wrap.appendChild(msg); wrap.appendChild(out);
  return wrap;
}
```

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your packet: Initial Model (p. 8)

1. Review all the climate factor ideas the class surfaced during the **Rumors** routine.
2. In your group, identify the **most likely causes of present climate change** on Earth.
3. Consider how those factors and the resulting climate change could result in the **climate displacements** we observed (Text 2).
4. Represent all your ideas in the form of a **model**: a labeled diagram with arrows from causes → temperature change → hazards → people.

It's OK if your model disagrees with other groups'. You'll confirm, refine, or change your ideas as you investigate each factor.
:::

```{=html}
<script>
(function() {
  var cards = [
    {text: "Earth's climate never changed before humans came along.", type: "Myth",
     explanation: "Climate has changed naturally many times: ice ages came and went, and Text 1 shows a slow natural cooling over about 1,000 years. That's why scientists compare today's change with past natural changes."},
    {text: "Before about 1850, Earth had been slowly cooling for centuries.", type: "Fact",

    {text: "The hole in the ozone layer is the main cause of global warming.", type: "Myth",
     explanation: "The ozone hole lets in more ultraviolet (UV) light, a different problem. Greenhouse gases like CO₂ trapping heat are the main cause of today's warming."},
    {text: "If this week is unusually cold where you live, global warming must not be real.", type: "Myth",

    {text: "Climate-related displacement only happens in faraway countries.", type: "Myth",
```
